text:
maya: Heads-up — monitoring alert: ~12% GPU capacity drop in us-west2 over the last 7m, inference error rate up (Xid/ECC) and enqueue latency increasing. :eyes:
infra-bot: Alert triggered: fleet-gpu-health > threshold (rule: gpu_ecc_xid_50m). Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.local/fleet/gpu-health
lee: On it. Pulling node list and recent prober results now.
sam: Any signs of NIC/TOR flaps? I saw bursty packet drops from rack-9 TOR at 09:12. Could be compounding kernel/GPU retries.
alex: Pasting quick kernel snippet from gpu-node-9a:
```
kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 45
nvidia: ECC corrected errors increased: 3 -> 47 in 5m
net_ratelimit: eth1: rx errors spike
```
maya: Autoscaler also reporting backpressure; can't immediately provision more GPUs due to quota and burst limits. We need short-term routing mitigations. :warning:
lee: Recommend isolating suspected racks. Which nodes show both nvlink/ECC and rx errors? Sending list in DM.
sam: Propose: mark rack-9 and rack-11 maintenance, migrate critical workloads to reserved-pool-2 and failover to us-central for read-only traffic. Spares are scarce but available in reserved pool.
alex: Running nvlink and NIC probes now — nvlink counters noisy, eth1 if_in_errors jumped. `ethtool -S eth1` shows rx_dropped up.
infra-bot: Runbook suggests: 1) divert low-priority jobs, 2) start graceful drain of suspected nodes, 3) pause scale-to-zero to avoid eviction storms.
maya: Agree. @ops-bot can you flip routing for inference-route-prod to prefer us-central failover for read-only workloads? :pray:
ops-bot: Route update applied: inference-route-prod preferring us-central (change-id: r-0x9ab). Expected traffic shift: ~9% within 2m.
lee: Starting rolling drains: `kubectl drain gpu-node-9a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — in progress. Will stagger to minimize evictions.
sam: Heads-up: draining will cause eviction spikes on short-running jobs — pausing KEDA scale-to-zero for inference namespace now to reduce churn.
maya: Paused. Also opening OEM support ticket for potential card-flake (ticket #OEM-6421) and attaching telemetry.
alex: Attaching telemetry snapshot to ticket and ops channel. If ECC/Xid rates don't fall after drains, schedule expedited rack swap tomorrow morning.
maya: Creating an incident record and prepping a customer-facing note if impact continues past 30m. Estimated reclaimed capacity after initial drains: +~6% in ~15m.
lee: Monitoring: queue length steady, error-rate trending down slightly after route change. Will post another update in 10m. :thumbsup:
